_about: Curated PhyTro reference table. Maps Open Food Facts additive tags (and ingredient keywords) to a concern level with a short, conservative reason and the source to check. Levels: high = banned/revoked by a major regulator or classified as a carcinogen hazard; moderate = restricted elsewhere, under active review, or a recognized hazard at common intakes; low = generally recognized as safe but some consumers choose to avoid. This is decision support, not medical advice. Review and extend with your team.

en:e127.name: Erythrosine (FD&C Red No. 3)
en:e127.reason: FDA revoked authorization for use in food in January 2025 (food compliance deadline January 15, 2027).

en:e171.name: Titanium dioxide
en:e171.reason: No longer authorized as a food additive in the EU since 2022 (genotoxicity could not be ruled out); still permitted as a color additive in the US.

en:e443.name: Brominated vegetable oil (BVO)
en:e443.reason: FDA revoked the regulation authorizing BVO in food in 2024.

en:e924.name: Potassium bromate
en:e924.reason: Listed under California Proposition 65 as a carcinogen; not permitted in EU foods.

en:e320.name: Butylated hydroxyanisole (BHA)
en:e320.reason: IARC Group 2B (possibly carcinogenic to humans); listed under California Proposition 65.

en:e250.name: Sodium nitrite
en:e250.reason: Used in processed meats; IARC classifies processed meat as Group 1 and ingested nitrite under conditions causing nitrosation as Group 2A.

en:e251.name: Sodium nitrate
en:e251.reason: Converted to nitrite; same processed-meat concern as E250.

en:e252.name: Potassium nitrate
en:e252.reason: Converted to nitrite; same processed-meat concern as E250.

en:e321.name: Butylated hydroxytoluene (BHT)
en:e321.reason: Synthetic antioxidant with mixed animal-study evidence; some consumers and retailers avoid it.

en:e951.name: Aspartame
en:e951.reason: IARC classified as Group 2B (possibly carcinogenic) in 2023; JECFA kept the acceptable daily intake at 40 mg/kg. Avoid if you have PKU.

en:e150d.name: Sulfite ammonia caramel (Caramel IV)
en:e150d.reason: Can contain 4-methylimidazole (4-MEI), which is listed under California Proposition 65.

en:e102.name: Tartrazine (Yellow 5)
en:e102.reason: Synthetic dye; EU requires a warning label about possible effects on activity and attention in children.

en:e110.name: Sunset Yellow (Yellow 6)
en:e110.reason: Synthetic dye; EU requires a warning label about possible effects on activity and attention in children.

en:e129.name: Allura Red (Red 40)
en:e129.reason: Synthetic dye; EU requires a warning label about possible effects on activity and attention in children.

en:e124.name: Ponceau 4R
en:e124.reason: Synthetic dye with an EU child-activity warning; not permitted in US foods.

en:e104.name: Quinoline yellow
en:e104.reason: Synthetic dye with an EU child-activity warning; not permitted in US foods.

en:e122.name: Carmoisine
en:e122.reason: Synthetic dye with an EU child-activity warning.

en:e133.name: Brilliant Blue (Blue 1)
en:e133.reason: Synthetic dye; permitted in US and EU. Some consumers avoid artificial colors.

en:e132.name: Indigotine (Blue 2)
en:e132.reason: Synthetic dye; permitted in US and EU. Some consumers avoid artificial colors.

en:e211.name: Sodium benzoate
en:e211.reason: Generally recognized as safe; can form small amounts of benzene when combined with vitamin C (ascorbic acid) under heat or light.

en:e407.name: Carrageenan
en:e407.reason: Permitted in US and EU; debated gut-inflammation research, and some consumers avoid it.

en:e433.name: Polysorbate 80
en:e433.reason: Permitted emulsifier; animal studies suggest effects on gut microbiota, human evidence limited.

en:e466.name: Carboxymethyl cellulose
en:e466.reason: Permitted emulsifier; early human studies suggest effects on gut microbiota.

en:e950.name: Acesulfame K
en:e950.reason: Approved non-nutritive sweetener; some consumers avoid artificial sweeteners.

en:e955.name: Sucralose
en:e955.reason: Approved non-nutritive sweetener; some recent studies question breakdown products at high heat.

en:e621.name: Monosodium glutamate (MSG)
en:e621.reason: FDA considers MSG generally recognized as safe; a minority of people report short-term sensitivity.
en:e621.source: FDA - Questions and Answers on MSG

en:e927a.name: Azodicarbonamide
en:e927a.reason: Dough conditioner permitted in the US but not in the EU; breakdown product semicarbazide raised concern.

en:e1520.name: Propylene glycol
en:e1520.reason: Generally recognized as safe at food levels.
